author: Nate Miller
title: Chris Sale fires three scoreless frames before rain delay
desc: Chris Sale gave up no runs on two hits and one walk while striking out five over three innings in Friday's 2-1 loss to the Cardinals.
impact: Sale appeared to be locked in on the mound Friday night before his outing was cut short after just three frames due to a lengthy weather delay. The ace lefty was obviously not involved in the decision of this one. Sale will take a 9-6 record with a sensational 2.20 ERA and 1.11 WHIP into his 10th All-Star appearance next week.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Tim Tawa drives in four runs Friday
desc: Tim Tawa went 3-for-4 with a home run and four RBI in the Diamondbacks 9-3 win over the Dodgers on Friday.
impact: Tawa broke a 2-2 tie with a two-run long ball in the fourth inning. He later added a pair of RBI singles as he takes advantage of seeing more playing time at first base moving forward.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Eduardo Rodriguez delivers quality start in win Friday
desc: Eduardo Rodriguez allowed two runs on seven hits over six innings with five strikeouts and one walk in a win on Friday against the Dodgers.
impact: Rodriguez allowed back-to-back home runs to Shohei Ohtani and Andy Pages to begin his night before he was able to settle in. He held the Dodgers scoreless the rest of his outing across six innings. He takes a stifling 2.29 ERA into the All-Star break.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Xander Bogaerts hits home run Friday
desc: Xander Bogaerts went 1-for-5 with a home run in the Padres 5-3 loss against the Blue Jays.
impact: Bogaerts got the scoring going early with a two-run blast in the first inning off Shane Bieber. He is now hitting .225 on the season with nine home runs and 37 RBI.

author: Ari Koslow
title: JP Sears takes loss Friday
desc: JP Sears allowed three runs on six hits over 4 1/3 innings with three strikeouts and one walk in a loss on Friday against the Blue Jays.
impact: Sears was removed in the fifth inning with two runners on base, both of whom went on to score. He'll carry a 5.03 ERA into the All-Star break.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Cole Young goes yard Friday
desc: Cole Young went 1-for-3 with a home run in the Mariners 7-2 loss against the Rays on Friday.
impact: Young has been one of the more consistent parts of a disappointing offense for Seattle over the first half of the season. He is up to 11 home runs on the season.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Luis Castillo takes loss Friday
desc: Luis Castillo allowed four runs on nine hits over five innings with four strikeouts and one walk in a loss on Friday against the Rays.
impact: Castillo was able to work around trouble early in the game. He later went on to allow three solo home runs. He'll enter the All-Star break with a 4.93 ERA.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Brandon Eisert traded to Pirates
desc: The Pittsburgh Pirates are acquiring infielder Jacob Gonzalez and left-handed reliever Brandon Eisert from the Chicago White Sox for the 34th pick in tomorrow's draft and left-handed reliever Jaden Woods.
impact: Eisert has posted a 5.93 ERA over 27 1/3 innings in the bullpen with the White Sox this season. He'll figure to step into a middle-relief role in the bullpen with Pittsburgh.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Jacob Gonzalez traded to Pirates
desc: The Pittsburgh Pirates are acquiring infielder Jacob Gonzalez and left-handed reliever Brandon Eisert from the Chicago White Sox for the 34th pick in Saturday's draft and left-handed reliever Jaden Woods.
impact: Gonzalez was recently optioned back to Triple-A with Munetaka Murakami activated from the injured list. He now lands a fresh start in the infield with the Pirates.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Shota Imanaga gives up one run in loss Friday
desc: Shota Imanaga allowed one run on seven hits and a walk while striking out five across five innings in Friday's 4-0 loss to the Cincinnati Reds.
impact: Imanaga's only mistake in the game came in the fifth inning, when he left a fastball up in the zone that Elly De La Cruz crushed over the left-center-field wall. Despite owning an 0-2 record in his last three starts, he's pitched well, giving up two runs or fewer in each outing. He owns a 4.17 ERA and 1.12 WHIP across 19 starts this season. He is not scheduled to pitch again before the All-Star break.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Sandy Alcantara punches out eight in loss Friday
desc: Sandy Alcantara allowed three runs on five hits and no walks while striking out eight across seven innings in Friday's 3-2 loss against the Cleveland Guardians.
impact: Alcantara gave up a two-run homer to Chase DeLauter in the fourth inning and a sacrifice fly to Travis Bazzana in the fifth for the Guardians' third run of the game. Outside of the homer, Alcantara was sharp, as he didn't issue a single walk and limited Cleveland to just five hits. He's been excellent in his two starts in July, posting a 2.40 ERA and 0.80 WHIP with 16 strikeouts in 15 innings. He is not scheduled to pitch again before the All-Star break.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Jakob Marsee logs stolen base Friday
desc: Jakob Marsee went 1-for-3 with a walk and a stolen base in Friday's 3-2 loss against the Cleveland Guardians.
impact: After posting a .170/.277/.250 slash line in June, Marsee has turned things around in July. He's recorded a base hit in six of his last seven games, putting together a .333/.484/.458 line with one homer this month. While Marsee has been tough to trust this year due to his inconsistency at the plate, he's worth adding in deeper leagues while he's hot. He also provides fantasy managers with speed, as he's up to 19 stolen bases on the year.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Esteury Ruiz swipes bag Friday
desc: Esteury Ruiz drew three walks and logged a stolen base in Friday's 3-2 loss against the Cleveland Guardians.
impact: Ruiz didn't record a base hit in his start on Friday, but he reached base safely three times and swiped a bag. He's been limited to 12 at-bats in July, yet he's already tallied four stolen bases, pushing his season total to 20. He's best left on waivers until he receives more consistent playing time.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Heriberto Hernandez goes deep Friday
desc: Heriberto Hernandez went 1-for-3 with a home run, a walk, one run scored and an RBI in Friday's 3-2 loss against the Cleveland Guardians.
impact: Hernandez hit a solo homer in the sixth inning off Parker Messick, giving the Miami Marlins their first run of the game. He's off to a terrific start in July, posting a .346/.452/1.038 slash line with five home runs. He's worth streaming in deeper leagues while he's riding this hot streak at the plate.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Leo Jimenez goes deep Friday
desc: Leo Jimenez went 1-for-3 with a solo home run in Friday's 3-2 loss against the Cleveland Guardians.
impact: Jimenez launched a 407-foot home run off Erik Sabrowski in the seventh, his second of the season. He's started in back-to-back games for the Miami Marlins and is starting to show what he can do at the plate, going 3-for-7 with a homer, two runs scored and two RBI over that stretch. He's posted a .292/.346/.583 slash line across his last 24 at-bats.
